doc.name: THE MOON
doc.title: THE PALE WATCHER
doc.blurb: Our own Moon three nights from full, the dark seas of old lava on its face and Tycho, the bright young crater, throwing rays across the south. It never twinkles; it turns once for every trip round us, so we only ever see this side. Waxing gibbous tonight (25 August 2026); on the 28th it goes copper in a total eclipse. The eyes are Tycho and Copernicus.
